critique: The timing now reads correctly as a very brief muzzle event: it is bright at 0.01 and cleanly gone by 0.08. The burst also has a stronger horizontal muzzle-direction bias and a hot yellow-white palette. However, it still appears as a tightly packed tube of overlapping soft circular blobs, rather than the preset thumbnail's sharp, violent explosive/starburst shape. The flash needs less particle crowding, much smaller/crisper visible elements, and a wider directional cone so separated energetic fragments radiate from a distinct ignition area.

suggestions.why: Reducing the initial burst density prevents the current solid pile of overlapping discs and reveals separated explosive fragments.
Smaller primary particles will replace the large bubble-like circles with finer, more energetic flash detail.
Removing feathering gives the burst sharper particle edges instead of the current soft cloud appearance.
A wider directional spread creates the required forceful flared/starburst silhouette while retaining the rightward muzzle direction.
